newsitem.title: USA: Continental Air moves to 60-day fuel hedging plan.
newsitem.headline: Continental Air moves to 60-day fuel hedging plan.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc, which had been applauded for successfully hedging against soaring jet fuel costs in 1996, said it will now shift towards a 60-day fuel hedging program.
Continental said it is moving back to a "more normal" 60-day hedge program for 1997. The airline said it is currently hedged about 70 days in advance.
Continental said it was "fairly cost attractive" to hedge fuel for the entire year in 1996 to "lock in" low fuel costs.
But hedging a year in advance is now less attractive, the company said.

"For 1997, oil prices have been up at the level they're at for quite a while. The hedge market is not in the same position as it was in. Peoples' expectations are that fuel prices are going to drop dramatically in the next six months, at least as reflected in the forward curve," Continental's chief financial officer Larry Kellner said in a media teleconference Tuesday.
Continental said it booked about $65 million in net fuel hedge gains in 1996. The airline does not expect to book significant hedge gains in 1997.
